summary: Taiki Mibu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from Ryukoku University by 2016. He was attested as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at Ryukoku University in 2015.

Taiko Yamasaki (1929–2025) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Koyasan University and under Bokushō Kanayama, later holding posts at Koyasan University and Shuchiin University.

Tainori Tanigawa (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Koyasan University and earned a Ph.D. from Toyo University by 1994. At Koyasan University, he was attested as associate professor (1980–1988) and professor (2005).
Taion Satomi (born 1909) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University until 1933. In 1972, he was attested as a professor at Minobusan Junior College.

Tairyo Makita (1912–2011) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936) and Bukkyo University. He was a professor at Kyoto University (~1957–1976), president of Saitama Institute of Technology (attested 2001), and held a post at Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University.
Tairyu Tsunoda (born 1960) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He was attested as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College in 1995 and as a professor at Komazawa University in 2015.
Taisei Iwata (born 1937) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He was attested as a lecturer at Rissho University in 1984 and as a professor at Otani University in 1996.

Taishu Tagami (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1977–2006) and was attested as an adjunct lecturer at Eastern Institute in 1990.
Taishun Mibu (1913–1980) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Taisho University until 1937 and later served as director (所長) at Taisho University from circa 1952 to 1980.

Taitetsu Unno (1929–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1947–1951) and the University of Tokyo (~1951–1968), and served as a professor at Smith College from circa 1971 to 2007.

Taixu (1890–1947) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Jichan (~1904–1907). He founded several institutes, including Minnan Buddhist Institute (1918), Wuchang Buddhist Institute (1922), and Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute (1930–1931), serving as leader of Minnan in 1927.
Tak Pui Sze is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. Sze completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen.
Takahiko Kameyama is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. In 2015, Kameyama was attested as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

Takamaro Shigaraki (1926–2014) studied at Ryukoku University (~1947–1956), where he became professor of Shin Buddhist Studies (1970) and president (1989–1995). A Buddhist studies scholar, he also served as chairman of Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai (~2007–2014).

Takamatsu Yoshie (1880–1940) studied at Matsumoto Fukashi High School, Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō (~1900–1902), Waseda University (~1902–1905), and the University of Paris (~1916–1920). He held a post at Waseda University from circa 1906 to 1940.

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Inoue was attested in 2003 as a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and holds a post as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Fukita studied at Taisho University and Bukkyo University under Shozen Kumoi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Heinz Bechert, and was attested as a lecturer at Bukkyo University in 1999.

Takanobu Takahashi (1951–2017) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held a post at Shitennoji University (~1988–1996) and served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo from circa 1996 to 2016.

Takanori Kimura (born 1947) studied at Komazawa University in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He was a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1979), a lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and chief priest at Kaichoji (attested 2003).

Takao Hayashi (born 1949), an Indology and history of science scholar, studied at Tohoku University (~1968–1977) and completed a PhD under David Pingree at Brown University (~1981–1985). He was Professor of History of Science at Doshisha University (~1989–2015).
